# Proposal: Live-Reload Hot Swap & Pre-Paint Theme Restore

> Companion journey dashboard (planned, not yet generated): `index.html` in this folder. See [tasks.md](./tasks.md).
>
> **Retroactive change:** the implementation was written before this proposal existed. These artifacts record the decisions that were made and track the remaining verification.

## Why

When the dev server (`serve-report.mjs`) live-reloads a report, the page flashes the default `light` theme before switching back to the user's theme. The scroll position is also often lost. This happens because every file change triggers a full `location.reload()`, and the saved theme is only re-applied at `DOMContentLoaded`, after the first paint. During active work, reports are rebuilt many times a minute, so the flash and scroll jumps make the live dashboard tiring to follow.

## What Changes

- **Pre-paint theme restore:** the report shell applies the saved theme (`localStorage` key `html_report_active_theme`) in `<head>` before any stylesheet renders. Reports with no saved theme still default to `light`.
- **In-place hot swap on live reload:** when a served report changes on disk, the dev server's injected client fetches the new HTML and morphs only `<main>` in place, like Vite's HMR, instead of reloading the tab. Theme, scroll position, and other page state are kept.
- **Safe fallback:** if `<head>` assets or any inline script changed, if the page has no `<main>`, or if the morph library can't be loaded (offline), the client does a full reload and then restores the previous scroll position.
- **Content re-hydration hook:** the runtime exposes a re-init entry point that re-runs content-level hydration (icons, TOC, code highlighting, dates, markdown links, Mermaid, space detection) after a swap.
- No **BREAKING** changes. Static `print`/`report` deliverables are unaffected, apart from gaining the pre-paint theme restore.

## Capabilities

### New Capabilities
- None.

### Modified Capabilities
- `report-generation-core`: the theme requirement now says a previously selected theme is restored before first paint. A new requirement says live reload must preserve theme and scroll position, with a defined fallback.

## Impact

- `skills/html-report/assets/template-shell.html`: early theme script in `<head>`.
- `skills/html-report/assets/report-runtime.js`: new `reinitReportContent()` export.
- `skills/html-report/scripts/serve-report.mjs`: rewritten `injectLiveReload()` client snippet (hot swap + fallback + scroll restore).
- New runtime dependency, dev server only: Idiomorph `0.7.3`, loaded on demand from jsDelivr (already allowed by the shell's CSP). It is never part of built reports.
- Existing built reports pick up the pre-paint script only after a rebuild. The hot swap applies to every page the dev server serves.

# Technical Design: Live-Reload Hot Swap & Pre-Paint Theme Restore

## Context

See [proposal.md](./proposal.md) (Why). Current state before this change:

- The [template-shell.html](../../../skills/html-report/assets/template-shell.html) hard-codes `<html data-theme="light">`. The runtime is inlined at the end of `<body>`, after the synchronous Tailwind CDN script, and restores `html_report_active_theme` in `scanAndRegisterExistingCustomThemes()` at `DOMContentLoaded`. So the first paint is always `light`.
- `injectLiveReload()` in `serve-report.mjs` listens on the `/__live_reload__` SSE stream and calls `window.location.reload()` on every `reload` event.
- Report content lives in a single `<main>`. Report-specific inline scripts (for example Chart.js setup) sit inside `<main>`, and the runtime script follows it.
- Constraint from the project: no npm or bundler for reports. Everything comes from CDNs, and the shell's CSP already allows `cdn.jsdelivr.net`.

## Goals / Non-Goals

**Goals:**
- No theme flash on any reload, whether hot or full.
- Keep the user's place (scroll, theme, open dropdowns) when only content changed.
- Never show stale or broken content: when unsure, fall back to a full reload.

**Non-Goals:**
- Re-running changed inline scripts in place (true module HMR).
- Preserving state inside JS-generated widgets whose *data* changed (charts, calendars, maps) without a full reload.
- Changing behaviour of static `print`/`report` deliverables beyond the pre-paint theme script.

## Decisions

### D1: Pre-paint theme script in `<head>` (before the DaisyUI stylesheet)
A tiny inline IIFE right after `<meta charset>` reads `html_report_active_theme` and sets `data-theme` on `<html>`. It runs before any CSS is applied, so the first frame is already correct.
- *Alternative: bake the theme into HTML at build time.* Rejected: the build can't see the browser's `localStorage`, and different viewers have different themes.
- *Alternative: hide the body until the runtime is ready.* Rejected: it swaps a colour flash for a blank flash and delays first paint.

### D2: Morph `<main>` with Idiomorph instead of reloading (Vite-style)
On `reload`, the client fetches the page (`cache: no-store`), parses it with `DOMParser`, and calls `Idiomorph.morph(currentMain, nextMain)`. Identical nodes stay in place, so focus, scroll and Alpine state survive.
- *Alternative: Vite.* Rejected: there is no "Vite CDN". Vite is a Node dev server plus bundler, which would add npm and a build step against the project's CDN-only constraint.
- *Alternative: `innerHTML` replacement of `<main>`.* Rejected: it destroys every node, including canvases holding live charts, and visibly flickers.
- *Alternative: Datastar fragment morphing.* Datastar is only loaded on `live-report` pages. Idiomorph is a ~3 KB on-demand load that works for every mode.

### D3: Safety signature decides hot swap vs. full reload
The client compares a signature of the *raw server HTML*: all `<head>` stylesheets, `script[src]`, `<style>`, and the text of every inline `<script>` (excluding the live-reload script). It compares against a baseline fetched when the page loads. If anything differs, it does a full reload.
- The signature is taken from raw HTML, never the live DOM, because Tailwind CDN and Mermaid inject `<style>` nodes at runtime and would make every comparison fail.

### D4: Preserve JS-generated widgets during morph
`beforeNodeMorphed` skips `<canvas>`, `.fc` (FullCalendar), `.leaflet-container`, `.gridjs-container`, and any element marked `data-hot-keep`. Their generated DOM would otherwise be reset to empty server markup. This is safe because D3 guarantees that the scripts driving them are unchanged.

### D5: Runtime re-init hook `reinitReportContent()`
After a morph, the client calls `window.reinitReportContent()`, which re-runs only content-level hydration: Lucide icons, TOC, highlight.js, Day.js, markdown auto-links, Mermaid (re-rendered from its stored source), and space detection. Navbar, theme and download wiring are left alone because they live outside `<main>`.

### D6: Scroll-restoring full-reload fallback
Before any fallback reload, the client stores `scrollY` in `sessionStorage` (one key per path). After the reload it sets `history.scrollRestoration = "manual"` and re-applies the position until `window.__REPORT_READY__` is set (capped at 4 s), so async chart and Mermaid layout shifts don't move the user.

## Risks / Trade-offs

- [Idiomorph CDN unreachable] → Falls back to the full reload with scroll restore (D6).
- [A JS-generated widget not in the D4 skip list gets reset by the morph] → Mark it `data-hot-keep`. A full browser refresh always recovers.
- [Content-only edits to `<main>` that a widget reads at init time (for example a `data-*` config on a canvas) won't re-initialise that widget] → Accepted for live preview; a manual refresh applies it. A later change could treat `data-*` changes on kept nodes as part of the signature.
- [Baseline fetch races a file write right after page load] → Worst case is one unnecessary full reload.
- [Rapid successive `reload` events] → Serialised: a busy flag queues at most one follow-up swap.

## Migration Plan

- No migration needed. The hot swap is live as soon as the dev server restarts.
- The pre-paint script reaches existing reports when they are rebuilt with `build-report.mjs`.
- Rollback: revert the three touched files. Nothing persistent changes apart from a transient `sessionStorage` key.

## 1. Pre-paint theme restore

- [x] 1.1 Add early inline theme script to `<head>` of `template-shell.html` that applies `html_report_active_theme` before CSS loads

## 2. In-place hot swap (dev server)

- [x] 2.1 Rewrite `injectLiveReload()` in `serve-report.mjs`: fetch the page, compare the raw-HTML safety signature, then morph `<main>` with Idiomorph 0.7.3 (loaded from CDN on demand)
- [x] 2.2 Skip morphing JS-generated widgets (`canvas`, `.fc`, `.leaflet-container`, `.gridjs-container`, `[data-hot-keep]`)

## 3. Fallback reload with scroll restore

- [x] 3.1 Save `scrollY` to `sessionStorage` before a fallback reload and restore it until `__REPORT_READY__` (4 s cap)

- [x] 4.1 Add and export `reinitReportContent()` in `report-runtime.js` (icons, TOC, hljs, Day.js, md links, Mermaid, space check)

## 5. Verification

- [x] 5.1 Syntax-check `serve-report.mjs`, `report-runtime.js`, and the injected client snippet
- [x] 5.2 Run the existing test suite (`node --test tests/*.test.mjs`) with no regressions (199/199 tests pass across all 18 test suites)
- [x] 5.3 E2E: content-only change keeps theme, scroll and page instance; TOC and Mermaid update
- [x] 5.4 E2E: inline-script change does a full reload and restores theme and scroll
- [x] 5.5 `openspec validate live-reload-hot-swap` passes

# Spec Delta: report-generation-core

## MODIFIED Requirements

### Requirement: DaisyUI Theme Dropdown with Default Light Theme, Color-Scheme Swatch Previews, and Live Chart Synchronization
Every generated HTML report SHALL default to the `light` DaisyUI theme (`<html data-theme="light">`), display all 32 built-in DaisyUI themes in a dropdown where each theme option previews its own color scheme (`bg-base-100`, `text-base-content`, and `bg-primary`, `bg-secondary`, `bg-accent`, `bg-neutral` swatches inside `data-theme="<theme>"`), and dynamically update Chart.js instances, Mermaid diagrams, and CSS-themed components when switching themes. When the user has previously selected a theme, the report SHALL restore that theme before the first paint, so the default theme is never briefly shown.

#### Scenario: Loading default light theme and selecting a DaisyUI theme with color swatches
- **WHEN** a report loads initially or a user selects a theme from the navbar dropdown
- **THEN** the initial theme is `light`, each dropdown item displays its 4 color swatches, `<html data-theme="...">` updates immediately, and all Chart.js, Mermaid, and Grid.js elements recompute their palette colors from the active DaisyUI theme variables

#### Scenario: Reloading a report after selecting a theme
- **GIVEN** the user previously selected the `dark` theme in a report
- **WHEN** the report is reloaded or reopened in the same browser
- **THEN** the first rendered frame already uses the `dark` theme, with no visible flash of the `light` theme

## ADDED Requirements

### Requirement: Live-Reload State Preservation
When the live-reload dev server detects a change to a served report and only the report's main content changed, the open tab SHALL update that content in place without a full page reload. The active theme, scroll position, and other client-side page state SHALL be kept.

#### Scenario: Content-only change while a themed, scrolled report is open
- **GIVEN** a report served by the dev server is open with the `dark` theme and scrolled partway down
- **WHEN** only text or markup inside the report's main content changes on disk
- **THEN** the tab shows the updated content without a full page reload, the theme stays `dark`, the scroll position is unchanged, and the Table of Contents and Mermaid diagrams reflect the new content

### Requirement: Live-Reload Fallback with Scroll Restoration
When an in-place update is not safe or not possible, the dev server's live-reload client SHALL fall back to a full page reload and SHALL then restore the previous scroll position and theme. This applies when `<head>` assets or inline scripts changed, when the page has no main content element, or when the in-place update mechanism is unavailable.

#### Scenario: Inline script change triggers fallback reload
- **GIVEN** a report served by the dev server is open with the `dark` theme and scrolled partway down
- **WHEN** an inline script or a `<head>` asset of the report changes on disk
- **THEN** the tab performs a full reload, the new script runs, and after load the theme is `dark` and the scroll position is restored to where it was

#### Scenario: In-place update mechanism unavailable
- **WHEN** a report changes on disk while the browser cannot load the in-place update mechanism (for example, offline)
- **THEN** the tab performs a full reload and restores the previous scroll position instead of failing silently
